questions.text: Is there any coordinating body or governance structure for digital health at any level, even if informal or constituted on a case-by-case basis?
Is a national digital health governance body formally constituted with a defined scope of work?
Does the digital health governance body conduct regular meetings at least quarterly with multi-stakeholder participation?
Does the digital health governance body actively monitor implementation of the national digital health strategy?
Is the digital health governance structure institutionalized, government-led, and reporting publicly on performance?
Is digital health included in any national health strategy or plan, even in an early or draft stage?
Has the proposed language for incorporating digital health into national health strategies or other relevant national plans been submitted and placed under official review?
Is digital health formally included in the national health strategy or other relevant national plans?
Is digital health actively being implemented as part of national health strategies and plans?
Is digital health periodically evaluated and optimized within national health strategies and plans?
Is there a high level of awareness regarding cybersecurity threats and vulnerabilities across the health sector, moving beyond initial discussions into active implementation?
Are there any cybersecurity awareness programmes, courses or resources available for health sector staff?
Is there a national cybersecurity awareness programme led by a designated health sector organisation?
Are metrics for cybersecurity awareness effectiveness established and evidence fed into future programmes?
Are cybersecurity awareness programmes adapted based on monitoring and performance evidence?
Has a national digital health strategy or framework been drafted, even if not yet officially approved?
Has a national digital health strategy or framework been officially approved?
Is there an approved national digital health costed implementation plan?
Is the national digital health strategy and costed plan at least partially implemented with resources secured?
Is the national digital health strategy and costed plan fully implemented with next cycle planning underway?
Is there a budget line item for digital health in the national budget, even if the proportion is not yet tracked?
Does public spending on digital health represent less than 1% of the annual health budget?
Does public spending on digital health represent between 1% and 3% of the annual health budget?
Does public spending on digital health represent between 3% and 5% of the annual health budget?
Does public spending on digital health represent more than 5% of the annual health budget?
Are established incentive structures currently available to support health system players?
Are specific incentives, such as tax benefits, actively available and accessible within the health sector?
Is the process for applying for incentives streamlined and user-friendly enough to ensure high usage among stakeholders?
Are health system players actively utilizing government grants and tax immunities to strengthen their core business models?
Are health system players systematically integrating advanced incentives, such as innovation parks and grand challenges, into their long-term business strategies?
Is there a formal legal foundation currently being established for data security in digital health?
Has a data security law relevant to digital health been drafted and progressed to the official review stage?
Has the data security law been officially enacted to provide a legal basis for digital health operations?
Is the data security law currently active and being integrated into digital health practices across the sector?
Is the data security law for digital health being consistently enforced and monitored to ensure full compliance?
Is there a formal process currently underway to establish legal protections for individual health data privacy and ownership?
Has a draft law governing the access and sharing of identifiable health data been successfully moved into the official review stage?
Has a comprehensive privacy law been officially enacted to provide a legal basis for protecting individual digital health data?
Is the legal framework for health data privacy currently being applied and integrated into digital health systems across the country?
Is the law protecting individual privacy and data ownership being consistently enforced and monitored to ensure full compliance?
Are there active efforts or discussions currently in place to develop frameworks for secure cross-border data exchange?
Have formal protocols and policies for cross-border data storage and exchange been drafted and submitted for official review?
Has a regulatory framework for cross-border data exchange been officially approved to enable secure regional data sharing?
Are the established protocols for cross-border data exchange currently being utilized and integrated into digital health operations?
Are cross-border data exchange policies being consistently enforced and monitored to ensure secure and standardized data storage?
Is there an increasing initiative to educate internet users/Digital health users on moving beyond blind trust toward a more cautious online presence?
Are there specific national programs or digital literacy surveys that track the population's ability to verify the authenticity of health information and practice safe online data management?"
Are user-consent policies effectively notifying users of data practices while a growing number of individuals actively identify online risks?
Do the majority of internet users possess the confidence to recognize non-legitimate websites and maintain control over their personal data?
Do individuals systematically assess the evolving cybersecurity environment and continuously adjust their online behavior to mitigate new risks?
Is the government actively initiating a secure environment to promote the foundation of future e-government services?
Do stakeholders and users officially recognize the security measures being applied to establish trust in expanding e-government services?
Is there a coordinated program in place that promotes e-government trust through compliance with privacy-protecting web standards?
Do most users trust and use secure e-government services supported by routine transparency and privacy-by-default tools?
Are data protection impact assessments consistently performed and integrated into the strategic planning of e-government services?
Is there an active effort to initiate discussions among public and private stakeholders regarding the protection of personal information?
Have stakeholders begun to adopt proactive cybersecurity practices while engaging in formal discussions to balance security and privacy?
Is there a growing proportion of users with the skills to manage their online privacy, supported by public debates that actively inform policy?
Do stakeholders widely recognize their privacy rights and possess the confidence to maintain control over the distribution of their personal data?
Are personal information protection assessments conducted regularly and used to refine policies based on user feedback and the changing risk environment?
Is there an active initiative to develop and integrate a digital health curriculum into the national pre-service training requirements?
Has a formal digital health curriculum for health professionals been drafted and submitted for official institutional review?
Is the digital health curriculum currently being launched, with active implementation starting in key health training institutions?
Do the majority of health training institutions now provide comprehensive digital health education as a core requirement for students?
Has digital health training achieved high-level saturation, reaching more than 75% of all health professionals during their pre-service education?
Is there an active initiative to develop and integrate digital health competencies into the national medical school curriculum for doctors/ physicians?
Has a formal digital health curriculum for doctors/physicians been drafted and submitted for official institutional review?
Has the implementation of the digital health curriculum successfully reached up to 25% of doctor/physicians in their pre-service training?
Is digital health currently being taught to a majority of doctors/physicians (between 50% and 75%) during their pre-service training?
Has digital health training achieved high-level saturation, with more than 75% of doctors/physicians receiving it in their pre-service education?
Is there an active initiative to develop and integrate digital health competencies into the national medical school curriculum for doctors/ physicians?
Has a formal digital health curriculum for nurses been drafted and submitted for official institutional review?
Has the implementation of the digital health curriculum successfully reached up to 25% of nurses in their pre-service training?
Is digital health currently being taught to a majority of nurses (between 50% and 75%) during their pre-service training?
Has digital health training achieved high-level saturation, with more than 75% of nurses receiving it in their pre-service education?
Is there an active initiative to develop and integrate digital health competencies into the national medical school curriculum for Community Health Workers (CHW)?
Has a formal digital health curriculum for Community Health Workers (CHW) been drafted and submitted for official institutional review?
Has the implementation of the digital health curriculum successfully reached up to 25% of Community Health Workers (CHW) in their pre-service training?
Is digital health currently being taught to a majority of Community Health Workers (CHW) (between 50% and 75%) during their pre-service training?
Has digital health training achieved high-level saturation, with more than 75% of Community Health Workers (CHW) receiving it in their pre-service education?
Are there active steps being taken to initiate a formal workforce strategy or policy that recognizes and organizes digital health roles?
Has a national needs assessment been completed that identifies the specific skills required for digital health, with an explicit focus on training female health workers?
Are digital health roles officially mapped to government career schemes, with 25% to 50% of the required public sector workforce currently in place?
Does an HR policy and strategic plan exist that focuses on training female health workers and has resulted in 50% to 75% of the digital health workforce being filled?
Is there a long-term plan and performance management system in place that has successfully filled more than 75% of digital health positions with low staff turnover?
Has the national Network Readiness Index (NRI) score successfully reached or exceeded a baseline of 1.0 to 3.3?
Has the country demonstrated moderate network readiness by achieving an NRI score greater than 3.3 (up to 4.0)?
Has the national infrastructure progressed to a solid NRI score of greater than 4.0 (up to 5.0)?
Is the country currently performing at a high level of network readiness with an NRI score greater than 5.0 (up to 5.4)?
Has the country achieved elite-level network readiness with a top-tier NRI score greater than 5.4 (up to 7.0)?
Has the national internet infrastructure successfully established a baseline coverage for up to 20% of the population?
Has the country expanded its digital reach to provide internet access for 20% to 40% of the population?
Is there consistent internet coverage available for 40% to 60% of the national population?
Has the country achieved high-level connectivity, reaching between 60% and 80% of all citizens?
Has the country reached near-universal connectivity with internet coverage exceeding 80% and approaching 100%?
Has the national mobile infrastructure successfully established a foundational baseline for connectivity?
Is 2G mobile connectivity currently available nationwide to support basic digital health communications?
Has the country successfully deployed 3G mobile broadband to enable basic data-driven health services?
Is high-speed 4G LTE mobile broadband widely available to support advanced digital health and data exchange?
Has the country achieved next-generation 5G connectivity to support high-performance digital health innovations?
Are any national priority health areas supported by digital health systems, even at pilot stage?
Are fewer than 25% of national priority health areas supported by scaled digital health systems?
Are 25–50% of national priority health areas supported by scaled digital health systems?
Are 50–75% of national priority health areas supported by scaled digital health systems?
Are more than 75% of national priority health areas supported by scaled digital health systems with M&E?
Is there any HIS governing body formally constituted, even if not fully functional?
Does the HIS governing body conduct regular meetings with stakeholder participation?
Does the HIS governing body use a work plan to monitor HIS interoperability implementation?
Is HIS governing body mobilizes resources (financial, human resources, and political) to accomplish its goals?
Is the HIS governing body legally protected and its work embedded in national law or policy?
Are there active efforts to move Big Data implementation from an ad hoc approach toward a structured national health framework?
Has the inclusion of Big Data been formally discussed and integrated into the drafting process for national health strategies?
Is Big Data officially recognized and included as a core component of the current national health or digital strategy?
Is the national Big Data strategy currently being actively implemented across the health sector to drive data-informed decisions?
Is the use of Big Data in health systematically evaluated and optimized to ensure it continuously improves national health outcomes?
Are there active efforts to move from fragmented local databases toward a federated architecture that allows data to be discoverable across different regions and levels of government?
Has a unified technical and legal framework been adopted that defines common data standards and "sharing contracts" between the national hub and sub-national nodes?
Do sub-national entities (regions/provinces) manage their own health data as "data products" that are high-quality, secure, and ready for authorized national or continental access?

Is there a standardized, self-service platform available that allows sub-national health offices to "plug in" their data systems to the national mesh with minimal manual configuration? (i.e., whether there is a centrally provided platform, toolkit, or service—such as APIs, onboarding portals, or integration templates—that enables regional or district systems to connect to the national system easily, without requiring extensive custom development or manual intervention from central teams. “Self-service” implies that sub-national teams can initiate and manage integration with limited external technical support.)

Are privacy and security policies automatically enforced through code across all levels, ensuring that data access remains compliant regardless of which sub-national node is providing the information?
Is there an active initiative to draft and implement foundational policies governing the use, transfer, and sharing of health data?
Has the government or health organization successfully established data sharing policies that cover a significant portion of its existing data assets?
Are there formalized policies and technical protocols in place that allow for the secure and seamless transfer of health data between internal departments?
Does a comprehensive policy framework exist that governs the secure use and transfer of health data with both internal and external stakeholders?
Are data sharing policies regularly reviewed and optimized to ensure they support real-time, secure interoperability across the entire health ecosystem?
Is there an active effort to incorporate formal privacy and security requirements into the foundational digital health framework?
Has a preliminary security approach been drafted that specifically outlines the protection of digital health data?
Does the digital health strategy align with national and international security policies, including a clear plan for implementation?
Are there comprehensive specifications in place for front-end, back-end, encryption, and physical security to protect the health data ecosystem?
Is there a formal mandate and operational plan to conduct routine security audits and maintenance as part of the core system lifecycle?
Is there a national document for data management procedures for the national HIS?
Are electronic data management procedures developed and documented in a nationally recognized document?
Is there a roadmap to migrate health data collection and reporting from paper to electronic systems?
Are national electronic data management processes published and disseminated with standard SOPs?
Is health data access and use continuously monitored with data management systems updated accordingly?
Is there an active initiative to draft foundational data ethics and privacy provisions specifically for the healthcare sector?
Has a formal regulatory framework addressing health data security, privacy, and ethics been drafted and submitted for review?
Has the national government officially approved a health-specific data regulatory framework or policy?
Are health data privacy laws fully implemented with clear operational guidelines, stakeholder sensitization, and consistent enforcement?
Is there a recognized national mechanism (e.g., a committee or working group) that routinely reviews and updates HIS data ethics policies?
Is there an active initiative to establish a formal training program for the digital health workforce?
Has a national digital health workforce needs assessment been completed with a formal plan to bridge identified training gaps?
Are professional digital health training programs currently producing graduates who are ready for national deployment?
Are trained digital health professionals actively deployed across the health system, with a plan to address remaining personnel gaps?
Does the country have a sufficient number of trained digital health professionals deployed to meet all national and sub-national health needs?
Is there an active initiative to establish a formal training program specifically for Health Informatics or Health Information Systems (HIS)?
Has a national informatics workforce needs assessment been conducted, with formal training options currently under development?
Is professional training in health informatics currently available and producing graduates who are ready for national or sub-national deployment?
Are specialized informatics professionals actively deployed within the health system, with a plan to address remaining essential personnel gaps?
Does the country have a sufficient number of trained health informatics professionals to fully support and sustain all national HIS needs?
Is there a digital health(eHealth) architectue framework and/or health information exchange (HIE)
Has a national digital health architecture or health information exchange (HIE) been proposed?
Is the national digital health architecture or HIE operable and providing core functions?
Does the government lead and enforce implementation of the national digital health architecture or HIE?
Does the national HIE provide seamless data exchange across all systems with M&E built in?
Are there any health information standards (messaging or transmission) currently in use, even partially?
Does the national framework include a comprehensive set of standards covering data exchange, security, privacy, and hardware?
Are health information standards formally mandated and being implemented nationally?
Are industry-based technical standards (HL7, FHIR, etc.) mandated and complied with across systems?
Are data standards routinely updated and actively used for health system monitoring and evaluation?
Is there an active initiative to develop a formal plan for the procurement and long-term maintenance of digital health equipment and software?
Has a comprehensive infrastructure plan (covering computers, tablets, and software) been officially approved and prepared for national rollout?
Has the infrastructure plan been launched, with at least 25% of the necessary digital health equipment currently in use and functional in the public sector?
Is there a consistent supply and maintenance system in place that has equipped between 25% and 50% of the public healthcare sector?
Has the country achieved high-level infrastructure maturity, with over 75% of the public sector equipped and receiving regular hardware and software upgrades?
Is there an active initiative to move from ad hoc tracking toward a formal, documented plan for HIS Monitoring and Evaluation?
Has a formal HIS M&E framework been developed that defines specific indicators for system performance, data quality, and user engagement?
Is the HIS M&E plan consistently implemented at the national level, with regular data collection on system health and performance?
Is the HIS M&E process government-led and fully operational at both national and sub-national levels to ensure consistent performance tracking?
Does the M&E data actively drive continuous system improvements, resource allocation, and policy updates for the national HIS?
Is there an active initiative to draft and approve a formal Business Continuity Plan (BCP) for the national and sub-national HIS?
Has a formal BCP been developed that clearly outlines the protocols for maintaining critical health information processes during a disruptive incident?
Has the BCP undergone a formal audit confirming that at least 50% of the planned resilience measures are currently operational?
Does a recent audit confirm that at least 75% of the business continuity measures are consistently implemented across the HIS?
Has the country achieved full HIS resilience, with audits confirming that 90–100% of the Business Continuity Plan is fully implemented and tested?
Is there an active initiative to enable health data to be exported or accessed outside of the specific application where it was originally collected?
Can the data be extracted and accessed by external systems, even if it currently requires specialized analysis software or proprietary tools?
Is all required health data stored in standard, machine-readable open formats (such as CSV, JSON, XML, or direct database access)?
Is the health data consistently accessible in real-time through a standardized API (Application Programming Interface)?
Is the data accessible via a secure, high-performance API that supports automated cross-border or continental data exchange?
Is there an active initiative to digitize paper-based health records into a formal electronic storage system?
Is the health data currently stored in digital formats (like PDFs or Scanned Images) that allow for basic electronic archiving and retrieval?
Has the system moved toward structured digital storage, such as searchable text files or spreadsheets, to facilitate data analysis?
Is the health data stored in high-performance, structured databases (like PostgreSQL) that support real-time querying and application integration?
Is the data stored in a highly available, cloud-native or distributed database environment that supports continental or National-scale data mesh operations?
Is there an active initiative to move beyond isolated source systems toward a unified national data integration strategy?
Does the system currently allow for the periodic export and manual integration of data from different health programs?
Has a central data warehouse or repository been established that supports the automatic, real-time aggregation and linking of health data?
Does the national data repository successfully integrate and link health data with relevant external data sources (e.g., civil registry, logistics, or climate data)?
Is the integration framework designed to support a federated data mesh, allowing for seamless real-time data exchange across continental and sub-national nodes?
Is there an active initiative to move from immediate data deletion toward a formal historical data retention policy?
Does the system currently store historical records, even if newer updates currently overwrite the previous values?
Are all data updates and new entries automatically appended with timestamps to preserve a chronological history of all previous values?
Is there a formal process to map new data schemas to older formats, ensuring that historical data remains usable as the system evolves?
Does the system maintain an immutable, fully versioned history that supports advanced longitudinal analysis and automated auditing?
Is there an active initiative to identify and map fragmented health data silos as a first step toward national interoperability?
Have at least some key national health databases successfully implemented interoperability standards to share data with other systems?
Is the majority of the national health information ecosystem currently interoperable and capable of automated data exchange?
Are all national health databases fully interoperable, allowing seamless data flow even when data remains stored in decentralized silos?
Has the country achieved a fully unified or virtually centralized health data environment that provides a single, comprehensive view of all health information?
Is there an active initiative to move from outdated legacy systems toward modern, standards-based digital health technologies?
Has the country successfully modernized at least 25% of its core health information systems to align with current industry standards?
Have at least half of the national health information systems been updated to modern, interoperable, and maintainable technologies?
Has the majority (at least 75%) of the digital health ecosystem been transitioned to modern software and hardware architectures?
Are all national health information systems currently operating on modern, supported, and scalable technology stacks?
Is there an active initiative to begin identifying and categorizing potential national-level cybersecurity incidents?
Have specific cybersecurity threats already been formally categorized and recorded as national-level incidents?
Is there a functional central registry in place for the real-time recording and tracking of all national-level cybersecurity incidents?
Are national incident registries systematically updated, with dedicated resources allocated for analyzing and prioritizing urgent threats?
Is the national incident identification process dynamically updated and adapted based on changes in the global and regional threat environment?
Is there an active initiative to formally define and document the core processes and digital tools for incident detection and resolution?
Have key incident response processes been identified and is there a plan to transition from ad-hoc training to a structured operational model?
Are incident response processes and tools fully documented and functional, with team members receiving regular training on core cybersecurity concepts?
Does the incident response team possess specialized accreditation, forensic capabilities, and a formal mechanism for coordinating with international counterparts?
Are advanced tools for zero-day vulnerability mitigation embedded in the organization, supported by regional cooperation and continuous process optimization?
Is there an active initiative to recognize cybersecurity as a standalone priority within the national critical infrastructure risk management framework?
Are physical and virtual access controls implemented across critical infrastructure, with a basic capacity to detect and respond to threats?
Have cybersecurity best practices and standards been adopted, with a formal national response plan that includes all vital health entities?
Is cybersecurity firmly embedded in general risk management, including regular impact assessments and specific protocols for insider threat detection?
Are regular audits conducted to assess system dependencies, with the results directly informing executive decision-making and long-term business planning?
Is there an active initiative to establish a formal, secure national registry for uniquely identifying individuals for health purposes?
Has a secure health registry been established, with active efforts to ensure it is regularly maintained and updated?
Is the secure registry currently in active use and does it successfully cover at least 25% of the relevant national population?
Has the secure registry reached a moderate scale, providing reliable identity data for 25% to 50% of the population?
Does the secure registry cover over 75% of the population, providing high-quality, curated, and current identity data for health-related use?
Is there an active initiative to implement an MPI that links patient records across disparate health information systems?
Has a functional MPI been established to manage cross-references between facilities, even if it currently requires manual data cleanup?
Is the MPI operational in a pilot or regional capacity, successfully linking patient records for at least 25% of the population?
Has the MPI reached a moderate scale, consistently deduplicating and matching patient records for 25% to 50% of the population?
Does the MPI provide a high-saturation service (>75% coverage) with automated, curated linking of patient records across the entire national health ecosystem?
Is there an active initiative to establish a formal, secure national registry for the electronic birth recording?
Has a secure eBirth registry been established, with efforts to ensure it is maintained and updated on a regular basis?
Is the secure eBirth registry in active use, successfully capturing at least 25% of all annual births at the national or sub-national level?
Has the eBirth registry reached a moderate scale, providing unique identification for 25% to 50% of the newborn population?
Does the eBirth registry cover over 75% of newborns, providing high-quality, curated, and current data for all health-related purposes?
Is there an active initiative to establish a formal, secure national registry for the electronic recording of deaths?
Has a secure death registry been established, with processes in place for its regular maintenance and updating?
Is the secure death registry in active use, successfully capturing at least 25% of all annual deaths at the national or sub-national level?
Has the death registry reached a moderate scale, covering between 25% and 50% of the relevant population?
Does the death registry cover over 75% of deaths, providing high-quality, curated, and current data for all health-related purposes?
Is there an active initiative to establish a formal, secure national electronic registry for tracking individual immunizations?
Has a secure immunization registry been established, with processes in place for regular data entry and maintenance?
Is the immunization registry in active use, successfully tracking vaccination records for at least 25% of the target population?
Has the immunization registry reached a moderate scale, providing unique records for 25% to 50% of the relevant population?
Does the immunization registry cover over 75% of the target population, providing high-quality, curated, and current data for public health action?
Is there an active initiative to identify and launch initial digital health or AI pilots to address specific public health challenges?
Does the country have a baseline of digital health pilots supported by various actors (IOs, NGOs, Gov), even if coordination between them is currently limited?
Have innovative pilots been brought under a formal organizational umbrella or coordination body to minimize duplication and maximize their value to the national system?
Is the coordinated pilot structure fully integrated into the larger ecosystem of scaled health solutions and cross-sectoral working groups?
Does a centralized platform exist to manage donor funding and strategic scaling, ensuring that successful pilots transition into national-level operational AI or digital solutions?
Is there an active initiative to develop protocols and frameworks governing the clinical use of connected medical devices and digital health services?
Have formal policies or frameworks for the regulation of digital health services (e.g., telemedicine) been drafted and submitted for official review?
Has a national regulatory framework for digital health and medical devices been officially passed into law or policy?
Is there a functional process in place for certifying digital health services and medical devices, even if enforcement is not yet fully consistent?
Are digital health services and connected devices consistently regulated and certified through a mature, nationwide enforcement and quality assurance process?
Is there an active initiative to explore the use of social media platforms for official health communication and public awareness?
Has a formal strategy been developed to guide the use of social media for health promotion and disease prevention?
Does the government extensively use social media channels to disseminate health information and official announcements to the public?
Are social media platforms integrated into broader public health campaigns for prevention, education, and multi-stakeholder information sharing?
Does the government actively analyze social media data to track health patterns, monitor public sentiment, and detect potential disease outbreaks?
Is there an active initiative to develop a digital health continuing education curriculum for the existing health workforce?
Has a formal digital health training framework for in-service professionals been drafted and submitted for official approval?
Is digital health training currently being delivered to a pilot group (up to 25%) of the active health workforce?
Has digital health training been successfully scaled to reach the majority (50% to 75%) of the national health workforce?
Is digital health a standard, mandatory component of continuing education for over 75% of all health and support professionals?
Is there an active initiative to develop a specialized digital health continuing education curriculum specifically for practicing doctors and physicians?
Has a formal digital health training framework for in-service physicians been drafted and submitted to medical boards or the Ministry of Health for review?
Is digital health training currently being delivered to a pilot group or a specific specialty (up to 25%) of the practicing physician workforce?
Has digital health training reached a significant scale, covering the majority (50% to 75%) of practicing doctors across the country?
Is digital health a standard, mandatory requirement for continuing medical education (CME) for over 75% of the national physician workforce?
Is there an active initiative to develop a specialized digital health continuing education curriculum specifically for practicing nurses?
Has a formal digital health training framework for in-service nurses been drafted and submitted for review to nursing councils or the Ministry of Health?
Is digital health training currently being delivered to a pilot group or specific nursing cadres (up to 25%) in the workforce?
Has digital health training reached a significant scale, covering the majority (50% to 75%) of nurses across the country?
Is digital health a standard, mandatory requirement for professional development and license renewal for over 75% of the national nursing workforce?
Is there an active initiative to develop a digital health training curriculum specifically for Community Health Workers (CHWs) already in the field?
Has a formal digital health training framework for in-service CHWs been drafted and submitted for approval to relevant health authorities?
Is digital health training currently being delivered to a pilot group (up to 25%) of the active CHW workforce?
Has the digital health training been successfully scaled to reach a majority (50% to 75%) of CHWs across the country?
Is digital health training a standard, mandatory requirement for over 75% of the national CHW workforce to ensure consistent data collection and service delivery?
Is there an active initiative to move beyond individual pilot adoptions toward a systematic process for integrating AI into the national health system?
Have government agencies and health system managers established a formal collaboration to provide guidance on AI health system integration?
Are there officially co-created national guidelines that outline the standards and protocols for integrating AI-driven solutions into the health sector?
Are AI solutions enabled through stepwise clinical protocols, updated workflows, and clear rules on equipment and information generation?
Are AI solutions fully integrated into clinical workflows as an essential pillar, with outcomes continuously measured to directly drive decision-making and Business Intelligence (BI)?
Are there any clinical decision support systems (CDSS) implemented in any healthcare workflow?
Are CDSS systems implemented across multiple clinical workflows in most facilities?
Are CDSS systems fully integrated with EMR/HMIS and updated with current clinical guidelines?
Are less than 20% of health services capable of being delivered or supported digitally?
Are 20–40% of health services capable of being delivered or supported digitally?
Are 40-60 % of health services capable of being delivered or supported digitally?
Are 60-80 % of health services capable of being delivered or supported digitally?
Are all core health services fully deliverable digitally with monitoring and evaluation built in?
Is there an active initiative to define and establish a national registry for uniquely identifying health providers and facilities?
Are the health system registries for providers and facilities currently being developed and prepopulated for future operational use?
Are the provider and facility registries available for use, even if the data is currently incomplete or updated irregularly?
Is the registry data regularly maintained and fully geo-tagged to enable active GIS mapping and spatial analysis?
Are the geo-tagged provider and facility registries utilized as a primary data source for national health strategic planning, budgeting, and service optimization?
Is health data management accountability defined but not centralized, with no national rules or standards?
Are policies in place to guide the governance, use, and management of health data and digital technologies?
Is there a national platform for managing health data, including rules, standards, and data quality processes?
Are national data stewardship guidelines established and aligned with international standards and policies?
Is data stewardship formalized and implemented with regular audits to enforce data policies and standards?
Is there an active initiative to sensitize leadership on how data can be leveraged to advance the organization's mission?
Has leadership expressed a formal commitment to using data, and is a roadmap being developed to integrate data into decision-making?
Does leadership consistently utilize data to drive strategic and operational decisions beyond just justifying donor funding?
Has a "data culture" been established where leadership requires data-backed evidence for all major programmatic and policy decisions?
Does leadership treat data as a strategic asset, using real-time Business Intelligence (BI) to continuously optimize health system performance?
Is there an active initiative to define formal, written procedures for how health data should be cleaned, analyzed, and interpreted?
Have initial data analysis protocols been drafted for specific programs (e.g., HIV or Malaria), even if a comprehensive national set is not yet complete?
Does a comprehensive manual of national data analysis procedures and policies exist and have official approval?
Are standardized data analysis procedures actively implemented and followed at both the regional and national levels of the health system?

Are standardized data analysis procedures consistently and routinely applied across all levels of the health system (facility, sub-national, and national), with evidence of sustained use in decision-making?
Is there an active initiative to train staff on the importance of data for achieving the organization’s health mission?
Does the organization have specific individuals or units who deeply understand the available data and its potential for improving health services?
Does the staff across the organization understand how to use data to drive operational decisions beyond just meeting donor requirements?
Is there a strong data culture where staff at all levels demand and use data to justify programmatic changes and policy shifts?
